3D volume of a domain

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/volume.R
volume.Rd

Measures the occupied volume of a SpatEnvelope, a SpatVoxel or SpatVector3D polygons, as a total, or cell by cell for envelopes and voxels. Envelopes and voxels describe a 3D domain over a 2D grid, but they store depth in dual roles, so each computes the vertical extent differently:

Usage

volume(x, per_cell = FALSE, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatEnvelope'
volume(x, per_cell = FALSE, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatVoxel'
volume(x, per_cell = FALSE, bounds = c("midpoint", "top"))

# S4 method for class 'SpatVector3D'
volume(x, per_cell = FALSE, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatRaster'
volume(x, per_cell = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A SpatEnvelope, a SpatVoxel, or SpatVector3D polygons. A bare SpatRaster is rejected; build one with as_envelope(), vect_to_envelope() or as_voxel() first. A netCDF file isn't accepted: describe it with as_proxy() and read one time step with as_voxel().

per_cell

FALSE (default) for the total volume, TRUE for the volume of each cell. Not for SpatVector3D polygons.

...

Arguments for the SpatVoxel method, which are an error for an envelope or polygons.

bounds

SpatVoxel only. What each depth level stands for vertically: "midpoint" (default) puts the slab edges halfway to each neighbouring level (the World Ocean Atlas convention); "top" treats the level as the top of its slab, so the slab runs down to the next level. Under "top" the deepest level has no next level and contributes no volume. Outer edges are clamped to range(depths) under both. Same argument, same meaning, as in envelope_to_voxel(). Not used for a voxel that carries its own depth edges (see SpatVoxel).

Value

With per_cell = FALSE, a number: the total volume in km³. With per_cell = TRUE, a single-layer SpatRaster named volume on the grid of x: the volume of each cell in km³, NA where x is absent (no depth interval, or no occupied level). Its sum is the total.

Details

SpatEnvelope

Depth is the cell value, and the interval is solid by construction. Volume is sum(cell_area * (depth_max - depth_min)) over present cells.

SpatVoxel

Depth is the layer index. Each occupied voxel contributes its cell area times the thickness of the slab its depth level stands for, so interior gaps are excluded rather than filled.

SpatVector3D polygons

Measured from the outlines, not a grid: each polygon's area on the WGS84 ellipsoid times depth_max - depth_min. Polygon edges are geodesics, so a polygon drawn along a grid's cell edges measures slightly differently from its envelope on that grid, whose cells are bounded by parallels. The time interval doesn't change the volume. The total adds up the polygons, so where they overlap the shared space is counted once for each; the overlap between two sets is volume(intersect_3d(x, y)). per_cell = TRUE is an error, since polygons have no cells; put them on a grid with vector3d_to_envelope() first. Points and lines have no volume, so they are an error; buffer_3d() turns them into polygons.

A voxel volume is quantized to the levels the voxel was sampled at, and a voxel built by envelope_to_voxel() counts a level as occupied on any overlap with the envelope. So a range of 0-100 m discretized onto 0, 50, 100, 150, 200 m occupies three levels spanning 0-150 m and reports more water than the envelope it came from. Coarse levels overstate; the error shrinks as the levels tighten around the range. Where an envelope's limits fall exactly on levels under bounds = "top", the two agree.

To measure the space two domains share, measure their intersection: volume(intersect_3d(a, b)).

With one envelope and one voxel, intersect_3d() places the envelope on the voxel's depth levels, so the overlap is measured on those levels while volume() of the envelope uses its own depth limits. To compare the two on the same levels, measure the envelope on them too: volume(envelope_to_voxel(a, depths(b), bounds = bounds, depth_bounds = depth_bounds(b)), bounds = bounds). Pass the same bounds to intersect_3d() and volume(); otherwise the overlap and the input volumes are measured on different slabs and don't add up.

See also

intersect_3d() for the space two domains share, which volume() then measures; intersects_3d() for whether two domains share any depth in each cell; SpatVolume for why the two representations dispatch separately.

Examples

fp <- terra::rast(nrows = 2, ncols = 2, xmin = 0, xmax = 2000,
                  ymin = 0, ymax = 2000,
                  crs = "+proj=laea +lat_0=0 +lon_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m")
terra::values(fp) <- c(1, 1, 1, NA)

# 2.5D: three 1 km² cells, each 0-200 m => 3 * 1 * 0.2 = 0.6 km³.
e <- as_envelope(fp, depth_min = 0, depth_max = 200)
volume(e)
#> [1] 0.6

# 3D: the same domain on three levels. The slabs are 50 m, 100 m and 50 m,
# so the discretized volume matches exactly here.
v <- envelope_to_voxel(e, depths = c(0, 100, 200))
volume(v)
#> [1] 0.6

# An interior gap is volume a voxel can drop and an envelope cannot.
gappy <- v
gappy[[2]] <- terra::setValues(terra::rast(v[[2]]), NA)
gappy <- as_voxel(gappy)
volume(gappy)
#> [1] 0.3
volume(voxel_to_envelope(gappy))
#> [1] 0.6

# Per cell: the fourth cell is outside the domain, so it is NA.
terra::values(volume(e, per_cell = TRUE))
#>      volume
#> [1,]    0.2
#> [2,]    0.2
#> [3,]    0.2
#> [4,]     NA

# Overlap with a second domain at 100-300 m: intersect, then measure.
b <- as_envelope(fp, depth_min = 100, depth_max = 300)
ov <- intersect_3d(e, b)
volume(ov)
#> [1] 0.3
terra::values(volume(ov, per_cell = TRUE))
#>      volume
#> [1,]    0.1
#> [2,]    0.1
#> [3,]    0.1
#> [4,]     NA

# Polygons: a 10 km circle from 10 to 60 m deep, about
# pi * 10^2 * 0.05 = 15.7 km³.
detection <- as_vector3d(data.frame(lon = 150, lat = -20, depth = 35))
volume(buffer_3d(detection, radius_km = 10, depth_window = 25))
#> [1] 15.70776
